recorded.prompt:q-record: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-record: 'every number in every version comes from data the program produced, collected once in a record.' Reference table: 'write every number from the record' / 'type a number from a screen'.
recorded.prompt:q-average: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-average: "That is an average over one discrete change. It is not the value of the next dollar"
recorded.prompt:q-audit: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-audit: "If a row had been written wrongly ... its own slacks would agree with it; the check, written separately from the data, would not."

recorded.rule: Q2 v2: a giveaway, read from the question's own text alone
recorded.prompt:q-record: Answer ONLY from this question's own text: its stem and its options. Use no knowledge of the subject at all; treat every term as a word you have never met. Pick an option only when the wording itself singles it out: it is longer or more specific than the others, it repeats words from the stem, the others carry absolute terms such as 'always' or 'never', the stem's grammar fits it alone, or it restates the stem. A cue decides only when it clearly singles out one option over every other; a weak cue, or one another option shares, decides nothing. Otherwise answer 'none'. Say which cue decided it, or that none did.
recorded.outcome:q-record: from the question's text alone, the reader picked none; the key is 'c'
recorded.because:q-record: Only a has an absolute, which leaves b, c and d with no cue to decide among them.

recorded.prompt:q-record:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-record:a: 'A memo typed by hand from a screen of output is how a plan's NPV ends up as $23,068k in one email and $23,086k in another.'
recorded.prompt:q-record:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-record:b: 'Printing fewer numbers does not fix that: each reader still needs theirs, and any number copied by hand can be copied wrong.'
recorded.prompt:q-record:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-record:d: 'Each writer reads the record and nothing else: no writer solves, queries the model or looks at a screen.' Also, the rule is 'One record per run'.
recorded.prompt:q-average:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-average:a: "It is not the value of the next dollar ... so nobody multiplies 0.415 by a different cut."
recorded.prompt:q-average:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-average:c: The ratio is computed as an average over one change. The marginal value "on a MILP is a step function; lessons 9.2.3 and 9.2.4 build that curve".
recorded.prompt:q-average:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-average:d: "so nobody multiplies 0.415 by a different cut". The ratio holds only for that one change.
recorded.prompt:q-audit:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-audit:a: "the model would have kept the wrong rule and its own slacks would agree with it"
recorded.prompt:q-audit:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-audit:b: The checks must "not trust the model". A wrongly written row is kept by the model, so OPTIMAL only means the model's own rows hold. Reference: "Don't: check the plan with the model that made it".
recorded.prompt:q-audit:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-audit:c: "'Same plan: True' is what one rerun on one machine showed. It is not a guarantee". A rerun uses the same possibly wrong rows.
